To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

obstructive sleep apnea and hypopnea are common in patients with wheezing, that the presence of obstructive sleep apnoea and/or hypopnea in wheezing subjects is related to the presence of daytime symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity, and that the severity of obstructive sleep hypopnea in children with wheezing correlates positively with the severity of wheezing.
obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and asthma are associated with impaired sleep and daytime sleepiness, and that OSA is associated with increased asthma symptoms and exacerbations.
obstructive sleep apnea is associated with recurrent wheezers and asthma and that the two disorders are associated with impaired sleep quality and daytime cognitive dysfunction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the pathophysiologic mechanisms that link obstructive SDB and asthma.
the effects of sleep‐disordered respiration on the quality of life of children with recurrent wheeziness or asthma.
the interactions of SDB and asthma in children and adolescents, and the effects of SDB on sleep quality in children with asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SDB and recurrent respiratory wheezing are associated with sleep disturbances and cognitive deficits in children and adults, and that the two disorders may interact in the pathogenesis of each other.
the presence of recurrent wheezing and/or asthma increases the likelihood that SDB will be present.
SDB, especially in children, may be associated with wheezing, asthma, and sleep disturbance and that asthma may be associated with sleep disturbance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SDB, recurrent wheezing, and asthma share many common pathophysiological mechanisms, and their coexistence may lead to more severe symptoms and worse quality of life.
obstructive sleep apnea is a risk factor for asthma, while asthma can lead to obstructive sleep‐apnea syndrome (OSAS).
SDB and recurrent asthma/wheezing are associated with sleep disturbances and daytime dysfunction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
obstructive SDB and recurrent episodes of wheezing/ asthma are both common and frequently co‐occur.
SDB and recurrent respiratory symptoms are common in children, with a substantial overlap between these two conditions.
SDB and recurrent asthma are associated with impaired sleep quality and daytime cognitive performance.
